reader.requirement: At --std 85, given the implementor's device transfer size (GR2; documented as one 80-character record, docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-5.md), an ACCEPT whose receiving item (any category, usage, group, reference-modified slice or ODO group at its current extent) is larger than a transfer stores each transfer left-aligned in the unoccupied portion and requests more (GR4a, level 2), and where a transfer exceeds the receiver or its remaining portion stores only the leftmost characters and ignores the rest (GR4b). Witnesses g85_z08 and g85_pb5856 cover X receivers of 5/80/100/170 characters and numeric receivers of every usage.
reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|DialectBehavior|IsActive|Edition|ConstructRegistry in AcceptDisplayEmitter.cs and AcceptSource.cs: no match; the device transfer is the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: not a group receiver, a reference-modified receiver, a JUSTIFIED receiver, an edited receiver, an ODO group at its current extent, a FROM mnemonic-name device

probes.printed: end of input on every ACCEPT (the run helper's stdin is the null device): G85[85 spaces]; R10[QQ    QQQQ] (only positions 3-6 replaced); JR[      ]; N4[+0000]; AE[   ]; ODO group with CNT=2: first 80 positions spaces, occurrence 3 still Q's
probes.expected: GR4a: the requested portion is filled from the transfers, end of input leaving spaces (DOC-A.1-5); the ODO receiver is its current extent, a slice only its own positions

probes.printed: Device(85) for the 85-char group, SpliceInto(R10,3,4,Device(4)), JR = Device(6) (left-aligned, no justification), DeviceNumeric(_P_5, 5, ...) for S9(4) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE, Device(3) for XBX, Device(OdoExtentChars(CNT...)) for the ODO group
probes.expected: each receiver requests exactly its own size in standard data format, so Device's record loop applies GR4a/GR4b to it

reader.notes: AcceptSource.Device reads 80-character records until the requested width is filled (GR4a) and keeps only the leftmost characters of the last record (GR4b); every receiver kind requests its own size. Doubt: run_probe.py gives the program a null stdin, so no probe could feed data; the data path was read in Device and in the generated code, and observed only at end of input. The witnesses g85_z08 and g85_pb5856 exercise the data path in the suite harness.

refuter.evidence: run_probe.py runs every program with stdin = DEVNULL (read in scripts/orchestrator/run_probe.py#main) and the CLI has no input option, so the data path cannot be probed through the one permitted helper; the verdict rests on reading AcceptSource.cs#Device and on the witness golden. Device loops on 80-character records until the requested width is filled (GR4a, left-aligned, each further record into the unoccupied positions) and returns the leftmost `width` characters (GR4b). Checked the witness conformance-suite/cases/VI.6.5@1985-ACCEPT-STATEMENT/g85_z08.in against g85_z08.out by hand: R170 from a 90-character line then 'C' -> 80 A, 10 B, 70 spaces, C, 9 spaces (GR4a over three transfers); R100 from 'WXYZ' then 'XY' -> WXYZ padded to 80 then XY (GR4a/b); R5 from a 100-character line -> ABCDE (GR4b). The one reading beyond the text: the second record of a line longer than 80 characters is discarded when the receiver took only the first (g85_z08 line 6 prints LAST). §1985:VI.6.5.4 GR4 governs one ACCEPT only and is silent on where the next ACCEPT's data begins; DOC-A.1-5 documents 'every ACCEPT begins at a new line', so it is an implementor choice outside this rule. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.5.4 GR4 ("the transferred data is stored aligned to the left").
